groups.title: Testing strategy for a full-stack PERN application
groups.question: Your PERN app has no tests yet, and you want confidence before each deploy without a slow, flaky suite. Explain which kinds of tests you'd write, how many of each, and how every developer would run them against the same database setup.

followUps.Testing pyramid: unit tests fast, integr: Why have many unit tests, fewer integration tests and only a few end-to-end tests?
followUps.Docker Compose for reproducible test env: How does Docker Compose make the integration tests behave the same on every machine?

evidence.text: Unit tests check small pieces alone, integration tests check pieces together with real dependencies like the database, and end-to-end tests drive the real app in a browser.
Lower levels are fast and stable, while higher levels give more confidence but are slower and flakier, so there are fewer of them.

notEnough: Only naming unit, integration and end-to-end tests without explaining the trade-off.

evidence.text: A compose file defines services like Node and PostgreSQL with fixed versions and settings.
Everyone starts the same environment with one command, so the tests don't depend on what is installed locally.

notEnough: Only saying use Docker without explaining what it makes reproducible.

groups.title: Container and CI/CD concepts
groups.question: You want every merge to main to test, build and deploy your API automatically as a small Docker image. Explain how the Dockerfile and the CI pipeline would be set up.

followUps.Multi-stage Dockerfiles for lean Node pr: How does a multi-stage Dockerfile make the final image smaller, and what gets left behind?
followUps.GitHub Actions workflow: test, build, an: In GitHub Actions, what triggers the workflow, in what order do the steps run, and where do the secrets come from?

evidence.text: A build stage installs all dependencies and compiles the code.
The final stage copies only the built output and the production dependencies, leaving build tools and dev dependencies behind.
The result is a smaller image that deploys faster and has less in it to attack.

notEnough: Only saying use multi-stage builds without saying what is copied.

evidence.text: A workflow runs on an event, such as a push to main.
Its steps run in order with tests first, so a failing test stops the build and the deploy.
Secrets are stored in the repository settings and passed to the steps as environment variables, never written in the workflow file.

notEnough: Only saying use GitHub Actions for CI/CD without describing the steps.

groups.title: Writing tests for the PERN stack
groups.question: You need tests for a date formatting helper, a Zod signup schema and the POST /posts endpoint that requires auth. Explain how you'd test each of them.

followUps.Vitest unit tests for utility functions: What edge cases would you test for the signup schema, and why are these tests so fast?
followUps.Supertest integration tests for Express: How does Supertest call your Express app in a test, and what would you check for the POST /posts endpoint?

evidence.text: Pure functions and schemas are tested by giving inputs and checking outputs, with no server or database.
Good tests cover edge cases, like an invalid email or a missing field being rejected by the schema.

notEnough: Only saying write unit tests with Vitest without saying what is checked.

evidence.text: Supertest sends real HTTP requests to the Express app inside the test process, without deploying it.
The test covers the whole path: validation, auth middleware, handler and database.
It checks status codes and response bodies, for example 401 without a token and 201 with valid input.

notEnough: Only saying test the endpoints with Supertest without saying what is checked.

groups.title: Deployment: React to Vercel, API to Railway, Postgres to managed host
groups.question: You're deploying your PERN app: the React frontend to Vercel, the Express API to Railway and PostgreSQL to a managed host. Explain the settings you'd configure, and how database changes are applied safely on each deploy.

followUps.Vercel project settings, build output, a: Vite environment variables are set in the Vercel dashboard. When do they take effect, and why must secrets never go there?
followUps.Running Prisma migrations in production: Why run prisma migrate deploy as part of the release, before the new API version starts?

evidence.text: Vercel needs the frontend's root folder, build command and output folder, like dist for Vite.
Frontend environment variables are baked into the bundle at build time, so changing one needs a redeploy.
Anything in the frontend bundle is visible to users, so it must not contain secrets.

notEnough: Only saying set the env vars in Vercel without explaining when they apply.

misconceptions.text: Says frontend environment variables can be changed at runtime without rebuilding.

evidence.text: Pending migrations are applied with prisma migrate deploy as a release step, before the new server starts.
That way the new code never runs against a database that is missing the tables or columns it expects.

notEnough: Only saying run the migrations in production without saying when or why.
